summary:
Queer-hostile offences recorded by Hessen police have risen in each year since 2022: 33 offences that year, 83 in 2023, 135 in 2024 and 141 in 2025, a more than fourfold increase across four years. Interior Minister Roman Poseck (CDU) called the development alarming in answers to Landtag inquiries from Grüne members and attributed part of the responsibility to far-right forces.

The 2024 figure, given in the interior ministry's answer to an August 2025 inquiry, was 52 higher than the previous year and comprised 16 cases of dangerous grievous bodily harm, seven of bodily harm, 13 of property damage and 26 of insult. Suspects were identified in 46 of the 2024 proceedings, and six convictions resulted.

Physical attacks form part of the record. Poseck cited a January 2026 incident on a Kassel tram in which a male couple was insulted, threatened and spat on for homophobic motives.

Frankfurt Airport produced a documented complaint by a trans traveller. On 23 November 2024 the DJ and producer BASHKKA was refused a search by a female officer during screening, and the male officer handling her told her she was 'not a woman'. She filed a complaint under the General Act on Equal Treatment. The airport apologised by email, said the security service provider had been instructed to investigate, and committed to training security staff on dealing with transgender and gender non-conforming travellers.
tangentialFactors:
The Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) situation report on the security of LSBTIQ* people, published with the Federal Interior Ministry, established the federal reporting category that makes comparison between Länder possible. The same report warns that changes in classification can inflate an individual Land's count, so cross-Land comparison of these figures requires caution. The Hessen totals are raw counts with no per-capita denominator attached.

Identity documents, legal gender recognition and anti-discrimination law are set at federal level in Germany and apply in Hessen without local variation. Hessen's own record consists of policing, courts and incidents.
localsOnly:
LSBTIQ* liaison officers have been established at every police headquarters in Hessen since 2010, under a framework concept governing their role.

Hessen police maintain dedicated contact officers for this category of hate crime, and the state government states that it pursues consistent prosecution of the offences.

Many victims do not report. The Hessian interior ministry assumes a high dark figure for queer-hostile offences, so recorded totals understate incidence by an unknown margin.
outOfScopeNotes:
Land-level totals depend on the federal reporting category, and the BKA notes that changes in classification can inflate them. The size of the gap between recorded offences and actual incidence is not sourced.

No Hessen-specific figures were identified for the placement of trans prisoners, access to health care, or the law governing access to sex-segregated facilities; those sit with the federal framework.

The outcome of the BASHKKA complaint is unresolved. Whether the security provider's investigation concluded and whether the promised staff training was delivered are not sourced.
